name: Tinfield 1
usage: Agentic coding and terminal work; fine-tune of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

licence.note: Follows the base model. The Q4_K_XL repository declares no licence in its metadata.

publisher.note: Small lab; earlier releases BTL-2-coder, BTL-3, BTL-4 and Macaw (June to August 2026). A Hacker News submission presents it as based in Nigeria (not checked).

size_gb.note: All builds from the publisher. Like the base model, they include the n-gram embedding table.

runtimes.value: llama.cpp with the GGUF builds; Transformers with the bf16 weights

fits_128gb.note: Compact (77.4 GB) and Mini (66.0 GB) fit; the Compact build ran on a DGX Spark 128 GB with llama.cpp, about 94 GB in use with four 128k slots. Q4_K_XL (111.3 GB) is tight. Not reported on Apple silicon.

web.verdict: Thin feedback: one sceptical comment on the self-reported scores; one independent run on a DGX Spark
web.summary: The publisher reports 33.0 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 62 on DeepSWE v1.1 for the bf16 weights, about 4 points above Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, measured by itself; the quantised builds were not evaluated. No independent check of these gains was found. The one comment on quality calls it a benchmark-tuned Qwen fine-tune. One independent measurement on a DGX Spark 128 GB (Compact build, llama.cpp) shows it runs well at 2 bits, with high tool and JSON scores and long thinking that can exhaust a token budget. No report on Apple silicon.
web.scope: Released on 21.09.2026 (under 3 months): all comments since the release. Read: Hacker News (comments of the only thread), Hugging Face discussions of the five repositories, GitHub issues and pull requests. Reddit could not be read (access refused to scripts).

speed.value: about 31 tok/s decode, one request; prompt 978 tok/s at 8k, about 520 tok/s at 160k

comments.text: Sees a Qwen fine-tune tuned for a few benchmark sets, far from beating Opus in real use, and reads the publisher's call for pre-seed investors as a reason to doubt the headline scores ([Reubend, 22.09.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49796378)).

Fine-tunes of existing models have value; an earlier model from the same publisher was awkward to run and needed a llama.cpp patch, the tooling seems to improve; waiting to see real performance ([kadoban, 22.09.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49796727)).

Praises the publisher for providing top-quality quantisations along with the fine-tune, and asks for its Q2_0 improvements to be contributed to llama.cpp ([Green-Sky, 23.09.2026](https://huggingface.co/badtheorylabs/Tinfield-1-Mini-GGUF/discussions/1)).

Compact build on a DGX Spark 128 GB with llama.cpp: tool use 0.988, JSON 0.982, instruction following 0.990, needle found up to 128k; coding 0.757 because 33 of 140 items spent the 4,096-token budget thinking (106 of the 107 finished items passed); one long-generation test returned nothing with thinking on, 0.972 with thinking off ([0xBakeer, inference-atlas #228, 21.09.2026](https://github.com/0xBakeer/inference-atlas/pull/228)).
